BC|PAOK]] | years18 = 2018–2019 | team18 = [[Eisbären Bremerhaven]] | years19 = 2019–2020 | team19 = [[Spójnia Stargard]] | years20 = 2020 | team20 = [[Stal Ostrów Wielkopolski]] | cyears1 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2019]]–present | cteam1 = [[ Big 3 - Detroit Amplifiers]] | highlights = * [[List of NCAA Men's Division I Basketball champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2008]]) }} '''Darnell Edred Jackson''' (born November 7, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player, who is currently an assistant coach for the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] of the [[NBA G League]] and plays in the Big 3 League for the Detroit Amplifiers. He played college basketball for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|University of Kansas]] for four seasons, including the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2008 national championship team]]. He did not become a regular [[Starting lineup|starter]] at Kansas until the [[2007-08 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2007–08 season]] (his senior year), when he replaced [[Sasha Kaun]] in the starting lineup. ==High school career== Jackson began playing organized basketball for the first time as a ninth grader at [[Midwest City High School]].[http://kuathletics.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jackson_darnell00.html Player Bio: Darnell Jackson :: Men's Basketball] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080216192340/http://kuathletics.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jackson_darnell00.html |date=February 16, 2008 }} Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Jackson was listed as the No. 12 power forward and the No. 54 player in the nation in 2004.[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Darnell-Jackson-13410;_ylt=AqFn3Tiq6eutU1eRjtJ5J6XXO5B4 Darnell Jackson Recruiting Profile] ==College career== He was called one of the most improved players in the nation after averaging 6.7 rebounds during his senior season at Kansas in 2007–08.{{Cite web |url=http://www.athlonsports.com/college-basketball/12788/hoops-notes-emotional-season-for-kus-jackson |title=Hoops notes: Emotional season for KU's Jackson – AthlonSports.com |access-date=January 26, 2008 |archive-date=March 27, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090327052402/http://www.athlonsports.com/college-basketball/12788/hoops-notes-emotional-season-for-kus-jackson |url-status=dead }} He attracted some attention from [[NBA]] scouts after several breakout performances, including a 25-point, 9-rebound effort against [[Boston College Eagles basketball|Boston College]]. After this performance, he was named the co-winner of the [[Phillips 66]] [[Big 12 Conference]] Player of the Week.[http://www.big12sports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/010708aaa.html Men's Basketball Weekly Honors Announced (Jan. 7) :: ] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20110526192416/http://www.big12sports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/010708aaa.html |date=May 26, 2011 }} In 2005, Jackson's sophomore year, Jackson was suspended for nine games for accepting payments from Kansas booster Don Davis, a family friend.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2225787 ESPN – Kansas F Jackson suspended nine games – Men's College Basketball] This was part of a rough year for him, as his grandmother had been killed by a drunk driver earlier in 2005. After scoring, Jackson often thumped his chest three times. Symbolically, one of the thumps was for Jackson's grandmother, one was for his mother, and one was for Davis.[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2006/jan/27/straight_heart/ KUsports.com – Straight from the heart] He played a big role in the Jayhawks' 2008 championship season, leading the team in rebounds and shooting percentage. ==Professional career== ===Drafted and signed by Cleveland=== Jackson was selected as the 52nd overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Miami Heat]] on June 26. He was traded to the Cavaliers on the same day. [[Sasha Kaun]], his former Jayhawks teammate and fellow 2008 draft pick, was also acquired by the Cavaliers (from the [[Seattle SuperSonics]]).[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/arthur_kaun_080626.html Cavaliers Acquire Draft Rights to Darnell Jackson and Sasha Kaun] Kaun was acquired by Cleveland during the 2015–2016 season, played in 25 games, and won a championship with the team.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3443/sasha-kaun|title=Sasha Kaun|website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 25, 2017}} Jackson was signed by the team on September 6, 2008.[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/darnell_jackson_080906.html Cavaliers Sign Darnell Jackson] ===2008 NBA Summer League=== Jackson played for the Cavaliers during the NBA (National Basketball Association) Summer League in [[Las Vegas, Nevada]]. In five games (four starts) he averaged 5.8 points and 5.4 rebounds in 24.6 minutes per game. ===2008–09=== Jackson broke his wrist during the preseason and was inactive for the first 13 games of the Cavaliers' regular season.[http://www.ohio.com/news/break_news/31235514.html Cavs rookie out with broken wrist] Jackson made his professional debut on November 25, 2008, against the [[New York Knicks]]. In six minutes of play, he scored four points on a perfect 2–2 from the field and grabbed two rebounds.[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3440/darnell-jackson Darnell Jackson Game Log] On February 9, 2009, Jackson was assigned by the Cavs to their affiliate D-League team, the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie Bayhawks]].[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/jackson_dleague_090209.html Darnell Jackson Assigned to Bayhawks] He played one game before being recalled back to the Cavs, a day later.[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/jackson_recalled_090210.html Cavaliers Recall Jackson from Bayhawks] In his only game with Erie, Jackson scored a game-high 24 points (on 10-of-14 field goals) in 26 minutes in a 101–89 win over [[Utah Flash|Utah]].[http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20090209/UTAERI/recap.html Jackson, Lafayette Lead Hawks Past Flash] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090213113514/http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20090209/UTAERI/recap.html |date=February 13, 2009 }} ===2009–10=== On February 24, 2010, Jackson was assigned to the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA D-League]].[http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/64980/20100224/cavs_send_green_jackson_to_d_league/ Cavs Send Green, Jackson To D-League] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100228140308/http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/64980/20100224/cavs_send_green_jackson_to_d_league |date=February 28, 2010 }} On February 26, 2010, Jackson was recalled by the Cavaliers after [[Shaquille O'Neal]] sustained a significant thumb injury against the [[Boston Celtics]] on February 25.{{cite news| url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/basketball/nba/02/26/cavaliers.jackson.ap/index.html?section=si_latest }}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Jackson was sent down again on March 20, and recalled the next day. On March 23, he was waived by Cleveland due to the return of star center [[Zydrunas Ilgauskas]].{{Cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5020973 |title = Ilgauskas signs with Cavs for rest of season|date = March 23, 2010}} He was then claimed off waivers by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Deprecated
